Let's be completely real for a moment. When generative AI first started blowing up, many graphic designers in Pakistan panicked. Freelance groups on Facebook were filled with posts saying, “Humari field khatam ho gayi” (Our field is over).

But at my agency, Media Initiation, we looked at it differently. We saw it as a way to stop spending hours hunting for the perfect royalty-free stock image on Freepik or Shutterstock—only to find out that another local brand had already used the exact same image on their billboard.

Over the last year, I have personally tested almost every major AI image generator Pakistan has access to. I've used them for real client projects, from designing packaging for local startups to creating social media grids for real estate clients in Islamabad.

If you are a Pakistani designer looking to add AI to your workflow without losing the “human touch” that clients actually pay for, this honest, unfiltered review is for you.

If you watch a Western tech YouTuber, they will show you how to generate a flawless, ultra-realistic image of a futuristic sci-fi city or a cyberpunk coffee shop. That's great for entertainment, but it doesn't help you when a local client comes to you and says:

“Mujhe apni brand ke liye ek Pakistani family chahiye jo Eid ke kapre pehan kar smile kar rahi ho.” (I need a Pakistani family wearing Eid clothes and smiling for my brand).

This is where most mainstream AI tools fall flat. They don't understand our culture, our traditional clothing (Shalwar Kameez), or our facial features. When you type “Pakistani man,” many tools mistakenly output images that look like generic Middle Eastern models or add strange, inaccurate cultural items.

To save you from wasting your internet data and time, I've broken down which platforms actually get our local context right.

If you want absolute jaw-dropping visual quality, Midjourney is still the undisputed champion in 2026.

We were designing a concept poster for a premium local clothing brand. They wanted a background that looked like an ancient, rustic Haveli in Lahore, bathed in moody evening light. Finding a stock photo like that with the right lighting is nearly impossible.

The Prompt I Used: A cinematic wide shot of an ancient Lahori Haveli courtyard, brick walls, traditional arches, soft golden hour sunlight, hyper-realistic, shot on 35mm lens –ar 16:9 The Result: It gave me four options that looked like high-budget movie sets. I picked the best one, brought it into Adobe Photoshop, cut out our local model, and blended her into the scene.

Yes, for art direction, it is unmatched. However, it has two major drawbacks for Pakistani freelancers:

If you are already paying for an Adobe Creative Cloud subscription on your laptop or PC, Adobe Firefly is integrated right inside your Photoshop and Illustrator panels.

The biggest issue with most AI image generators in Pakistan is copyright. If you use a tool that scraped random art from Pinterest to train its AI, your client could technically face legal issues later if they use that asset in a major commercial product.

Adobe Firefly is trained exclusively on licensed images and public domain content.

If you have a decent gaming PC or laptop (something with an Nvidia RTX card like a 3060 or 4060) and want a completely free AI image-generation workflow in Pakistan, Stable Diffusion is our best friend.

Unlike Midjourney, you can download Stable Diffusion models directly onto your local storage device and run them completely offline without paying a single Rupee.

Finding the right AI image generator in Pakistan comes down to knowing what your business needs. If you have the budget, Midjourney offers beautiful cinematic visuals. If you need clean production integration, Adobe Firefly is standard. If you love deep customization and have a powerful computer, Stable Diffusion gives you absolute control for free.

Don't let the technology intimidate you. Use these generators to speed up your mood boards, create stunning concept boards, and fix stock image issues. Keep practicing image issues in Illustrator, refine your composition skills in Photoshop, and use AI to handle the tedious tasks.

#9669. This fall, reach for this unlikely apple ingredient : Apple cider vinegar is a baker’s secret weapon.

As fall baking season settles in, you're probably reaching for apples — and the many flavor-packed ingredients they produce. Applesauce cooks down into tangy apple butter to be cradled in a flaky galette, while a drop of boiled cider can deliver supercharged apple flavor to crumb cake. But the baking ingredient you may be overlooking may be something you associate more with salad dressings and wellness tonics: apple cider vinegar.

This tangy, apple-y vinegar is a secret ingredient in some of our favorite fall recipes, including cookbook author Claire Saffitz’s Cinnamon-and-Sugar Apple Pie. While lemon juice is the standard acid used in most fruit pie fillings, Claire opts for apple cider vinegar here to complement the filling’s flavors. “It helps as a flavor enhancer, and I also like that it’s apple cider in an apple pie. It’s a nice symmetry,” she mentions.

Similarly, apple cider vinegar is used in the cooking liquid alongside sugar and butter to caramelize apples in a Classic Apple Tarte Tatin. The benefit is twofold: Vinegar’s acidity helps cut the sweetness of the caramel, and it prevents the apples from getting too mushy, instead maintaining their fork-tender texture.

Pastry chef and cookbook author Natasha Pickowicz often leans into the jolt vinegar can add, including adding a few drops to her cake soaks for an additional layer of flavor. “Cake soaks should have a balance of tart, sweet, and savory notes — just like vinaigrette for your favorite salad,” she writes in her cookbook More Than Cake. It can add intrigue to layered cakes like this Golden Spice Cake or Pumpkin Layer Cake. In her cookbook, she also calls for a glaze spiked with apple cider vinegar to brush onto an apple tart after baking. It’s the finishing touch “to further emphasize the tart’s resolute apple-ness,” she writes.

Apple cider vinegar doesn’t need to be limited to only apple desserts, either. In our Old-Fashioned Pecan Pie, we call for apple cider vinegar as a foil to the brown sugar filling’s cloying sweetness. A spoonful of apple cider vinegar may not announce itself boldly, but it makes a small splash for brighter, more balanced bakes.

#9668. Canva Review 2022: Details, Pricing & Features


Are you looking for a new graphic design tool? Would you like to read a detailed review of Canva? As it's one of the tools I love using. I am also writing my first ebook using canva and publish it soon on my site you can download it is free.  Let's start the review.

Canva has a web version and also a mobile app

What is Canva?

Canva is a free graphic design web application that allows you to create invitations, business cards, flyers, lesson plans, banners, and more using professionally designed templates. You can upload your own photos from your computer or from Google Drive, and add them to Canva's templates using a simple drag-and-drop interface. It's like having a basic version of Photoshop that doesn't require Graphic designing knowledge to use. It’s best for nongraphic designers.

Who is Canva best suited for?

Canva is a great tool for small business owners, online entrepreneurs, and marketers who don’t have the time and want to edit quickly.

To create sophisticated graphics, a tool such as Photoshop can is ideal. To use it, you’ll need to learn its hundreds of features, get familiar with the software, and it’s best to have a good background in design, too.

Also running the latest version of Photoshop you need a high-end computer.

So here  Canva takes place, with Canva you can do all that with drag-and-drop feature. It’s also easier to use and free. Also an even-more-affordable paid version is available for $12.95 per month.

Free vs Pro vs Enterprise Pricing plan

The product is available in three plans: Free, Pro ($12.99/month per user or  $119.99/year for up to 5 people), and Enterprise ($30 per user per month, minimum 25 people).

Free plan Features

  • 250,000+ free templates
  • 100+ design types (social media posts, presentations, letters, and more)
  • Hundreds of thousands of free photos and graphics
  • Invite members to your team
  • Collaborate and comment in real-time
  • 5GB of cloud storage
  • Try Canva Pro for free for 30 days

Pro Plan Features 

  • Everything Free, has plus:
  • 100+ million premium and  stock photos, videos, audio, and graphics
  • 610,000+ premium and free templates with new designs daily
  • Access to Background Remover and Magic Resize
  •  Create a library of your brand or campaign's colors, logos, and fonts with up to 100 Brand Kits
  • Remove image backgrounds instantly with background remover
  • Resize designs infinitely with Magic Resize
  • Save designs as templates for your team to use
  • 100GB of cloud storage
  • Schedule social media content to 8 platforms

Enterprise Plan Features

  • Everything Pro has plus:
  • Establish your brand's visual identity with logos, colors and fonts across multiple Brand Kits
  • Control your team's access to apps, graphics, logos, colors and fonts with brand controls
  • Built-in workflows to get approval on your designs
  • Set which elements your team can edit and stay on brand with template locking
  • Unlimited Storage
  • Log in with single-sign on (SSO) and have access to 24/7 Enterprise-level support.

How to Use Canva?

To get started on Canva, you will need to create an account by providing your email address, Google, Facebook or Apple credentials. You will then choose your account type between student, teacher, small business, large company, non-profit, or personal. Based on your choice of account type, templates will be recommended to you.

You can sign up for a free trial of Canva Pro, or you can start with the free version to get a sense of whether it’s the right graphic design tool for your needs.

Canva Sign Up

Designing with Canva



When you sign up for an account, Canva will suggest different post types to choose from. Based on the type of account you set up  you'll be able to see templates categorized by the following categories: social media posts, documents, presentations, marketing, events, ads, launch your business, build your online brand, etc.

 Start by choosing a template for your post or searching for something more specific. Search by social network name to see a list of post types on each network.

Templates



Next, you can choose a template. Choose from hundreds of templates that are ready to go, with customizable photos, text, and other elements.

You can start your design by choosing from a variety of ready-made templates, searching for a template matching your needs, or working with a blank template.

To begin with, Canva has a large library of elements to choose from. To find them, be specific in your search query. You may also want to search in the following tabs to see various elements separately:

Photos

The Photos tab lets you search for and choose from millions of professional stock photos for your templates.

You can replace the photos in our templates to create a new look. This can also make the template more suited to your industry.

You can find photos on other stock photography sites like pexel, pixabay and many more or simply upload your own photos.


When you choose an image, Canva’s photo editing features let you adjust the photo’s settings (brightness, contrast, saturation, etc.), crop, or animate it.

Text

The Text tab lets you add headings, normal text, and graphical text to your design.

When you click on  text, you'll see options to adjust the font, font size, color, format, spacing, and text effects (like shadows). 

Canva Pro subscribers can choose from a large library of fonts on the Brand Kit or the Styles tab. Enterprise-level controls ensure that visual content remains on-brand, no matter how many people are working on it.

Audio

Create an animated image or video by adding audio to capture user’s attention in social news feeds.

If you want to use audio from another stock site or your own audio tracks, you can upload them in the Uploads tab or from the more option.

Video

Once you have chosen a video, you can use the editing features in Canva to trim the video, flip it, and adjust its transparency.

Backgrounds

Styles


The Styles tab lets you quickly change the look and feel of your template with just a click. And if you have a Canva Pro subscription, you can upload your brand’s custom colors and fonts to ensure designs stay on brand.

Logos

If you have a Canva Pro subscription, you’ll have a Logos tab. Here, you can upload variations of your brand logo to use throughout your designs.

With Canva, you can also create your own logos. Note that you cannot trademark a logo with stock content in it.

Publishing with Canva

With Canva, free users can download and share designs to multiple platforms including Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Slack and Tumblr.

Canva Pro subscribers can create multiple post formats from one design. For example, you can start by designing an Instagram post, and Canva's Magic Resizer can resize it for other networks, Stories, Reels, and other formats.

Canva Pro subscribers can also use Canva’s Content Planner to post content on eight different accounts on Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Slack, and Tumblr.

Canva Team

Canva Pro allows you to work with your team on visual content. Designs can be created inside Canva, and then sent to your team members for approval. Everyone can make comments, edits, revisions, and keep track via the version history.

Canva Print

When it comes to printing your designs, Canva has you covered. With an extensive selection of printing options, they can turn your designs into anything from banners and wall art to mugs and t-shirts. 

Canva Print is perfect for any business seeking to make a lasting impression. Create inspiring designs people will want to wear, keep, and share. Hand out custom business cards that leave a lasting impression on customers' minds.

Canva Apps

The Canva app is available on the Apple App Store and Google Play. The Canva app has earned a 4.9 out of five star rating from over 946.3K Apple users and a 4.5 out of five star rating from over 6,996,708 Google users.

In addition to mobile apps, you can use Canva’s integration with other Internet services to add images and text from sources like Google Maps, Emojis, photos from Google Drive and Dropbox, YouTube videos, Flickr photos, Bitmojis, and other popular visual content elements.

Canva Pros and Cons

Pros:

  • A user-friendly interface
  • Canva is a great tool for people who want to create professional graphics but don’t have graphic design skills.
  • Hundreds of templates, so you'll never have to start from scratch.
  • Wide variety of templates to fit multiple uses
  • Branding kits to keep your team consistent with the brand colors and fonts
  • Creating visual content on the go
  • You can find royalty free images, audio, and video without having to subscribe to another service.

Cons:

  • Some professional templates are available for Pro user only
  • Advanced photo editing features like blurring or erasing a specific area are missing.
  • Some elements that fall outside of a design are tricky to retrieve.
  • Features (like Canva presentations) could use some improvement.
  • If you are a regular user of Adobe products, you might find Canva's features limited.
  • Prefers to work with vectors. Especially logos.
  • Expensive enterprise pricing

Conclusion

In general, Canva is an excellent tool for those who need simple images for projects. If you are a graphic designer with experience, you will find Canva’s platform lacking in customization and advanced features – particularly vectors. But if you have little design experience, you will find Canva easier to use than advanced graphic design tools like Adobe Photoshop or Illustrator for most projects. #9667. What Happens to Your Digital Accounts After a Chargeback?

Former banker (25 yrs) & economist dissecting crypto security, wallet UX flaws, DeFi risks, payment cards, and how banks actually work.

Former banker (25 yrs) & economist dissecting crypto security, wallet UX flaws, DeFi risks, payment cards, and how banks actually work.

Former banker (25 yrs) & economist dissecting crypto security, wallet UX flaws, DeFi risks, payment cards, and how banks actually work.

Your issuing bank will happily hand your 50 USD back. What the representative on the phone will rarely mention is that once those funds are clawed back, the merchant on the other side of the trade holds sweeping contractual rights over your account. When that merchant happens to run your cloud storage, your smart home, your decade-old gaming library, or your daily ride to work, a minor billing victory can turn into a painful digital lockout overnight.

After 25 years in traditional banking, I cringe every time I hear social media finance gurus repeat their favorite piece of lazy advice: "If customer support gives you a hard time about a refund, just call your credit card company and file a chargeback." People treat the bank dispute button like a VIP customer service hotline. It is nothing of the sort. Inside the plumbing of global card rails, a chargeback is a forced financial extraction. You are asking your bank to reach directly into a merchant's settlement balance, pull the cash back over the card network, trigger a punitive dispute fee, and log a blemish against their compliance metrics with Visa or Mastercard.

Do that to a neighborhood dry cleaner and they might ban you from the shop. Do that to Apple, Google, Sony, Valve, Microsoft, Amazon, or Uber over a 20 USD subscription renewal, and you are rolling the dice with automated risk engines that control far more than a single receipt. At best, your profile gets hit with an unpaid balance lock or a payment verification hold; at worst, if the platform flags the reversal as payment abuse or unauthorized activity, you can win a 20 USD battle at your bank only to lose access to thousands of dollars in purchased media, connected devices, or cloud workflows.

To understand why tech platforms treat bank disputes so seriously, you have to understand the legal and operational chasm between a refund and a chargeback. During a standard refund, the merchant voluntarily pushes money back to your card over the payment rails. During a chargeback, your issuing bank forcibly reverses the transaction through the card network's dispute machinery, bypassing the merchant's checkout support entirely.

Consumers often assume that when their bank rules in their favor, the case is closed and the merchant has to respect the verdict. That is a costly misunderstanding of how commercial law works. Your bank adjudicates whether you owe the money on your monthly card statement; the tech platform adjudicates whether you are allowed to use its servers under its terms of service. When you pull the trigger on a dispute, your money and your account standing can quickly start moving in opposite directions.

In the United States, consumer banking protections are remarkably strong on paper. For credit cards, the Fair Credit Billing Act (implemented through Regulation Z) gives you the legal right to challenge billing errors and unauthorized charges. According to the CFPB's official credit card dispute rules, as long as you send written notice within 60 calendar days after the error first appeared on your statement, the card issuer must investigate and pause collection on the disputed charge (often issuing a temporary credit) while the case plays out. Debit cards carry separate protections for unauthorized electronic fund transfers under Regulation E's error resolution framework.

Here is the catch that catches everyday users off guard. Regulation Z and Regulation E bind your bank, not the merchant. Zero federal statutes force a private corporation to keep extending services to a customer who just reversed a settled payment.

Worse yet, consumers increasingly lean on bank disputes for what the payments industry calls first-party fraud, or "friendly fraud." According to Mastercard's 2026 chargeback outlook, global chargeback volume is projected to reach 334 million disputes annually by 2028, while merchants report that 21% of chargebacks are linked to first-party fraud, ranging from unrecognized or forgotten charges to intentional misuse of the dispute process. Separate Mastercard-sponsored research with Javelin found that for 75% of disputes, consumers go straight to their card issuer without contacting the merchant first. Because issuing banks often find it cheaper to credit small disputes automatically than to investigate them manually, cardholders get lulled into thinking the tactic is consequence-free.

Of course, if a thief steals your physical wallet or hijacks your account, you must call your bank immediately and freeze the card. My warning here applies to using bank disputes as a casual shortcut to resolve everyday billing friction with ecosystems you cannot afford to lose.

If you want to know why a trillion-dollar company will freeze purchases or restrict an account over a 19.99 USD charge, stop looking at the customer support department and look at the treasury and risk desk. Every card transaction travels along a four-party rail: you (the cardholder), your issuing bank (such as Chase or Capital One), the card network (Visa or Mastercard), and the merchant's acquiring bank or payment processor (such as Stripe, Adyen, or J.P. Morgan Merchant Services).

When you initiate a chargeback, a costly chain reaction hits the merchant's back office:

Put yourself in the shoes of a platform risk officer looking at that math. A customer who files a 20 USD chargeback has just inflicted over 100 USD in combined direct and operational losses on the company. From a pure risk-management standpoint, letting an account rack up bank reversals unchecked makes zero financial sense.

The direct fees are only half the story. The deeper reason merchants aggressively police chargebacks is card network compliance enforcement. Visa and Mastercard track dispute and fraud ratios across every merchant portfolio on their rails.

In recent years, Visa overhauled its legacy compliance rules and consolidated five separate fraud and dispute tracks into a single framework: the Visa Acquirer Monitoring Program (VAMP). Under the official VAMP threshold schedule, Visa calculates a merchant's monthly ratio by combining TC40 fraud notices and TC15 non-fraud disputes divided by total settled card-not-present VisaNet transactions, with the U.S. Excessive Merchant threshold tightening to 1.5% (alongside at least 1,500 monthly combined fraud and dispute notices) in April 2026. Even if a merchant fights a chargeback and wins, that dispute still counts toward their monthly monitoring ratio.

Mastercard enforces a parallel framework called the Excessive Chargeback Program (ECP). As outlined in Stripe's card network monitoring guide, crossing both the 1.5% rate and 100-chargeback monthly count places a merchant into official remediation, with escalating monthly fines kicking in from the second consecutive month unless the ratio drops back below threshold. Payment processors simultaneously protect themselves from elevated dispute activity by holding a portion of a merchant's payouts in fixed or rolling reserves, as detailed in Stripe's merchant reserve policies.

Crossing a Visa or Mastercard monitoring threshold does not automatically terminate a merchant or blacklist the business overnight; the programs are built around mandatory remediation plans and escalating fees first. However, if a smaller vendor fails to bring its dispute levels down in time, the card network can eventually stop processing its payments, or its acquiring bank may terminate the account. As documented in Stripe's guide to terminated merchant files, once an acquirer terminates a merchant that meets specific network reporting criteria, such as Mastercard's MATCH Reason Code 04 (exceeding a 1% monthly Mastercard chargeback ratio and 5,000 USD in chargebacks within the same calendar month) or Visa's VMSS thresholds, the acquirer must report the business to those five-year high-risk databases, making it nearly impossible to open a new card-processing account elsewhere.

Even for giants like Sony, Apple, or Amazon, keeping ratios clean across dozens of regional merchant descriptors requires tight automated controls. Depending on how their fraud models classify a reversal, their systems will either lock new spending until the unpaid balance is cleared or quarantine the account for a security review.

Platforms do not react identically to every chargeback, and it helps to separate routine billing enforcement from worst-case account bans. Routinely, a single reversed payment creates an unpaid balance on your profile, revokes the specific item you disputed, or pauses new purchases until you settle the tab or verify your card. Contractually, however, every major tech ecosystem reserves broad authority to suspend or terminate accounts, and when an automated fraud model classifies a chargeback as unauthorized activity or payment abuse, the blast radius can hit your entire digital profile.

Gaming platforms enforce some of the strictest automated chargeback rules in the consumer economy, though each handles the boundary between a single revoked purchase and a full account lock differently.

Sony leaves very little wiggle room in its public rules. Under the PlayStation Network account debt and suspension policy, because a bank reversal can signal suspected fraud or an account takeover, Sony suspends the PSN account (or console) to investigate, displaying error codes WS-37368-7 or WS-116367-4 and restricting access to online services. If there was no lawful right to a refund, your PSN profile remains suspended until you repay the owed balance through Sony's recovery form, cutting you off from PlayStation Store purchases, online multiplayer, and PSN-authenticated features in the meantime.

Microsoft separates baseline chargeback handling from fraud enforcement across Xbox and Windows services. While Microsoft provides an official Xbox digital game refund portal for standard refund requests, bypassing Microsoft via your bank triggers Section 9.g of the Microsoft Services Agreement: Microsoft deems you to have canceled the service as of the original payment date and is authorized to immediately cancel that service and revoke the content provided for that payment. That is the routine baseline. However, if Xbox's risk systems determine that a chargeback or refund pattern crosses into fraudulent marketplace theft, Xbox Safety enforcement can escalate to temporary or permanent account and console bans, and Section 4.b.iv of the Services Agreement warns that permanent closure can forfeit your content licenses, memberships, and Microsoft account balances.

Think about how much of your daily digital routine runs through your Apple Account (formerly Apple ID). Under the Apple Media Services Terms and Conditions, you remain personally liable for any uncollected amounts, and Apple reserves broad authority to suspend or terminate access to its services or your Apple Account if you breach the agreement.

In everyday practice, Apple's documentation points to two distinct tiers of friction. If a failed or reversed payment simply leaves an unpaid order on your profile, Apple's unpaid balance support guide states that you might be unable to make new purchases, download free apps, or use subscriptions (and as noted in Apple's Mac App Store troubleshooting guide, an unpaid order can also block you from downloading or updating apps). In these routine unpaid-balance cases, manual intervention is not required: you can clear the balance yourself by adding a new valid payment method, which Apple charges automatically, or by redeeming an Apple Gift Card and applying the credit to the unpaid order in your purchase history.

However, if a chargeback or repeated billing dispute triggers an anti-fraud lock that disables your purchasing privileges outright, self-service card updates will no longer fix the problem. As shown in Apple's disabled Media & Purchases recovery guide, seeing the alert that your Media & Purchases account has been disabled means you have to request reactivation directly through Apple Support.

Google routes consumer and business billing through a shared hub: your Google Payments profile. As explained in Google's payments center documentation, that profile stores the cards, receipts, and recurring subscriptions behind Google Play, YouTube, Google One storage, hardware orders, and business tools.

A consumer chargeback does not automatically wipe out your Google Account or shut off Gmail on the spot. Instead, under the Google Pay and Google Payments U.S. Terms and Google's declined-transaction rules, when unusual or suspicious payment activity flags your payments profile, Google can block new purchases until you complete identity and payment verification, which may involve confirming a 6-digit temporary charge code or uploading images of a government ID and the payment card. If you also run ad campaigns on that account, Google Ads' billing suspension policy explicitly warns that instructing your bank to reverse a legitimate ad balance may result in your Google Ads account being paused or suspended.

For everyday users, the real danger of an unresolved payments-profile lock is the delayed domino effect on cloud storage. Under Google One's renewal and cancellation policies, if auto-renewal fails on your storage plan, Google provides a seven-day grace period to update your payment information. If a locked payments profile or unresolved billing dispute keeps your plan from renewing past that window and your usage sits above the free 15 GB quota, your Google Account stays accessible, but Google Photos stops backing up videos and pictures, Google Drive blocks new uploads and Workspace file creation, and Gmail stops sending and receiving messages, returning incoming emails to the sender. Leave an account over quota for two years or longer, and Google states your content may be deleted.

Amazon is no longer just a retailer that ships cardboard boxes to your porch; it also runs media libraries and smart-home devices tied to the same login. On routine marketplace disputes, Amazon's A-to-z Guarantee rules explicitly note that filing a credit card chargeback disqualifies that order from A-to-z Guarantee refund coverage, and ordinary payment declines usually just pause pending orders until you supply another card.

The stakes jump sharply, however, if a reversed charge or disputed card causes Amazon's risk models to flag your profile for unusual payment activity. Under Amazon's Conditions of Use, the company reserves broad discretion to refuse service or terminate accounts. More specifically, Amazon's Account on Hold policy states in plain English that when unusual payment activity triggers a temporary security hold on your account, your access to all Amazon services is also placed on hold during the review, explicitly listing Amazon Prime, Amazon Music, Kindle, and devices like Alexa and Ring. Until you sign into Amazon's secure portal and submit its verification form with the requested supporting attachments, your shopping account and connected digital services stay frozen together.

Uber illustrates a similar single-wallet bottleneck in daily transit and food delivery. Under Uber's U.S. Terms of Use, Uber retains sole discretion to deny access to or terminate any of its services at any time. In day-to-day operations, when a failed or reversed payment leaves an unpaid balance on your account, Uber's rider pending-amount rules and the matching Uber Eats outstanding-charge policy warn that you may be unable to request a ride or place a food order until you settle the pending charge in the app with a valid payment method (or arrange cash payment where supported).

Stepping back and looking at this friction through the lens of payment architecture reveals a striking irony. For decades, traditional bankers criticized cryptocurrency protocols because on-chain transactions are final and irreversible, whereas legacy credit cards offer consumer reversibility.

Yet in practice, credit card settlement finality is an illusion that encourages digital feudalism. When you swipe a Visa card, the merchant receives provisional funds within a couple of business days, but the transaction lacks true finality for months while card-network dispute windows remain open. Because centralized platforms cannot fully trust the finality of legacy fiat payment rails, they protect their balance sheets by tying your digital identity, subscriptions, and device ecosystems to a single revocable login.

In the crypto and Web3 world, we live by a simple rule: not your keys, not your coins. If you leave your digital assets on a centralized exchange, you do not hold bearer Bitcoin or stablecoins; you hold a revocable database entry that the exchange can freeze the moment a compliance or billing review flares up.

The exact same custody trap governs Web2 walled gardens. Not your servers, not your files. Even when you click the purchase button on an e-book, Amazon's Kindle Store terms of use explicitly state that digital content is licensed to you, not sold. When you bundle your primary email address, your cloud drive, your smart-home cameras, and thousands of dollars of revocable media licenses inside the same single sign-on profile that processes your credit card, you hand the platform enormous leverage. Your bank can force the merchant to return 50 USD, and the merchant retains the contractual power to freeze your billing profile, halt subscriptions, or, in severe enforcement cases, cut off access to thousands of dollars in licensed media.

In commercial banking, putting all of your operational liquidity and custody inside a single counterparty that can freeze your operations over a minor billing dispute is called concentration risk. No competent corporate treasurer would allow it, yet everyday consumers build their digital lives that way by default.

If you want to protect your money from bad billing without handing Big Tech unnecessary leverage over your accounts, follow these five operational rules.

If an unfamiliar storefront scams you on a pair of shoes from a random social media ad, file a chargeback without hesitation. However, if you are fighting a 30 USD charge from Apple, Google, Amazon, Sony, or Valve, treat the bank dispute button as a last resort. Exhaust the platform's internal refund escalation channels, reach out to executive customer relations, or file a formal complaint with the Better Business Bureau or your state Attorney General's consumer protection division first. Track your 60-day statutory bank deadline on the calendar so you never forfeit your legal rights under Regulation Z or Regulation E, but push the merchant to resolve the billing error internally whenever an essential account is on the line.

The cleanest way to win a billing dispute is to stop an unwanted charge at the authorization gate before the money ever settles. Once a charge settles, reversing it through your bank creates a chargeback; stopping an unwanted renewal at authorization simply triggers a routine "payment declined, please update your billing method" notice.

If you have thousands of dollars invested in a PlayStation, Steam, Xbox, or Apple library, leaving a live credit card or PayPal billing agreement on file means an accidental click, a child's in-game purchase, or a forgotten renewal can quickly turn into a high-stakes billing mess.

Instead, fund those wallets with prepaid store gift cards purchased from reputable retailers and remove live cards where possible. That way, the platform cannot pull more than the prepaid balance sitting in your wallet. Keep one practical rule in mind: under Apple's payment method removal policy, you must keep at least one payment method on file if you maintain active subscriptions like iCloud+, owe an unpaid balance, or serve as a Family Sharing organizer with purchase sharing enabled. Even then, keeping your Apple Account funded with gift cards helps ensure your prepaid balance absorbs routine charges before a backup card is touched.

Stop using the same Google or Apple account that holds your tax returns, family photo archives, and two-factor authentication recovery emails to test sketchy app trials or shared household entertainment. Build an air gap between your core infrastructure and your discretionary spending. Keep your primary email and cloud storage on a clean, dedicated account paid by a reliable card used strictly for storage infrastructure, and maintain a separate secondary account for media purchases, trials, and gaming.

Never confuse cloud syncing with an independent backup. If a payment verification hold or account suspension disrupts your Google, Microsoft, or Apple services tomorrow morning, any document or photo sitting exclusively inside a single cloud drive is exposed to single-provider risk. Keep local, encrypted backups of your critical documents, family photos, and password vaults on external drives you physically control, and make sure your two-factor authentication recovery codes are never stored solely inside the email inbox they are meant to unlock.

If you are reading this because you already filed a bank dispute and ran into a restricted PlayStation, Steam, Apple, or Google account, stop panicking and do not file a second dispute. Restoring access requires a careful reconciliation sequence between your bank and the merchant:

Consumer chargeback rights remain an essential safeguard against criminal fraud and rogue merchants. Use them without hesitation when a stranger steals your card details or a fly-by-night storefront takes your money and vanishes. Just understand how the payment rails and platform contracts actually interact before you fire that weapon at an ecosystem holding the keys to your digital life.

5 Banking Compliance Risks Every Independent Contractor Needs to Understand

#9666. What is high-extraction flour, exactly?  : A baker’s guide to our new T85 Baker's Reserve Bread Flour.

High-extraction flour is a technical term that often prompts a lot of confusion from those unfamiliar with it. But with the debut of our new high-extraction flour, known as Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour, we’re breaking down just what it is and why it's a great choice for avid bread makers.

The extraction rate of a flour refers to how much of the original grain — the bran, germ, and endosperm — ends up in the final flour. A high-extraction flour typically has an extraction rate of about 80% to 90%, meaning some of the bran and germ have been sifted out, but it still retains much of the original grain. Our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour is a T85 flour, meaning its extraction rate is 85%.

To put that in perspective, whole wheat flour has an extraction rate of 100%; it retains the entirety of the grain, including the bran, germ, and endosperm.

High-extraction flour falls between white and whole wheat flour. It’s lighter and less coarse than whole wheat flour because some of the bran has been sifted out, but it still retains more flavor, nutrients, and color than white flour, since it retains much of the original grain.

High-extraction flour is popular for artisan bread baking because it offers a balance of nutrition and good gluten development. It’s great for rustic loaves, baguettes, and pizza dough, and particularly well-suited for sourdough baking because it strikes a balance between flavor, nutrition, fermentation, and dough strength.

You can substitute our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour 1:1 for bread flour (by weight or volume) in artisanal bread recipes; it can also be used 1:1 to replace the total flour in recipes that call for a combination of all-purpose and whole wheat flour. If you're subbing Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour for all-purpose flour in a bread recipe, you may find you need to add slightly more liquid to the recipe.

Bread bakers love high-extraction flour for artisan bread and sourdough because it offers the flavor and nutrition of whole grain flour; the stronger gluten development and more open crumb you get from white flour; and better fermentation from the minerals present in the bran and germ, which feed the wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria in sourdough starter, promoting more active fermentation.

If you want a loaf of bread that’s more flavorful and nutritious than bread made with exclusively white flour, but that still rises high and has an open crumb, high-extraction flour is a great choice.

Yes — in fact, it’s a great choice for feeding starter because of the sourdough-friendly minerals present in the flour, which boost activity in your starter.

Yes! T85 is a French specification that refers to the extraction rate (85%) of the flour. Our Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour is a T85 flour, meaning the extraction rate is 85%. If you have a recipe that calls for T85, this flour is the perfect choice.

Find our high-extraction Baker’s Reserve Bread Flour online.

#9663. Diagnosing Slow SQL Server Queries: A Practical Guide to Query Store and Execution Plans

Driving database innovation, optimizing data architecture, and scaling database performance to ensure reliability, security, and operational

Driving database innovation, optimizing data architecture, and scaling database performance to ensure reliability, security, and operational

Driving database innovation, optimizing data architecture, and scaling database performance to ensure reliability, security, and operational

Most slow-query investigations start in the wrong place: a CPU alert fires, someone opens the plan cache, and whatever is running right now gets tuned. That finds the loudest query, not necessarily the costliest one, and it says nothing about what changed.

Query Store supplies the missing piece: historical visibility. It records query text, execution plans, and runtime statistics over time intervals. Because this information is persisted in the user database, it survives SQL Server restarts. Execution plans then help explain why a particular query is slow.

This article covers a practical troubleshooting workflow for SQL Server 2016 and later:

Every example uses T-SQL. Replace the sample database names and identifiers with values from your own environment.

Query Store is available starting with SQL Server 2016. SQL Server 2022 enables it by default for newly created databases, but existing databases and upgraded environments should still be checked.

Next, configure its operating parameters:

For SQL Server 2017 and later, enable wait statistics capture separately:

These values are starting points, not universal production recommendations. Adjust the storage limit and retention period according to workload volume, query diversity, and monitoring requirements.

A useful habit is to verify Query Store's state periodically:

If actual_state_desc differs from desired_state_desc, investigate why Query Store is not operating as expected.

Start with one question: Which queries consumed the most resources over the last 24 hours?

Query A looks worse when examining individual execution time. However, Query B may consume considerably more cumulative resources.

Query Store records average runtime statistics and execution counts for individual intervals. Multiplying the averages by execution counts provides an estimate of cumulative consumption.

The following query identifies the top 10 queries by total execution duration:

A few details matter when interpreting these results:

The time filter uses interval boundaries, so it can include executions from an interval that began before the exact 24-hour cutoff. The results are therefore an interval-based approximation rather than an exact rolling 24-hour measurement.

Run the query three times, changing the final ordering:

Queries appearing in multiple lists deserve closer investigation.

The SSMS Top Resource Consuming Queries report provides a graphical view of similar information. However, keeping a reusable SQL script makes it easier to automate reporting and compare workload trends over time.

A query that suddenly becomes slower without an application code change often deserves a plan investigation.

Query Store allows you to compare execution plans associated with the same query. First, identify the relevant query_id from the previous step. Then examine its historical plans.

This query calculates execution-count-weighted average duration and logical reads for each plan over the selected interval window.

These numbers are illustrative, but they show the kind of regression worth investigating.

Plan 23 takes considerably longer and performs significantly more logical reads.

The next step is to establish when the change occurred and correlate it with:

SQL Server Management Studio also provides the Regressed Queries report, which helps visualize performance changes and compare execution plans side by side. An important distinction: a different plan is not automatically a bad plan. The objective is to identify whether the plan change explains the observed performance degradation.

Query Store preserves compiled execution plans, but these plans generally contain estimated row counts rather than actual runtime row counts. For actual execution information, capture an actual execution plan by rerunning the query with Include Actual Execution Plan enabled in SSMS.

On SQL Server 2019 and later, you can also enable last-query-plan statistics:

The sys.dm_exec_query_plan_stats function can then provide the last known actual execution plan for a cached plan handle.

Remember that this is last-execution information, not a complete historical collection of actual execution plans.

When examining an execution plan, I recommend following this order.

One of the most useful indicators is the difference between estimated and actual row counts.

The optimizer expected approximately 100 rows but encountered 12,000.

That difference can influence downstream decisions, including join selection, memory grants, and parallelism.

A significant estimation difference is a diagnostic clue, not automatic proof that statistics are the problem.

Parameter sniffing occurs when SQL Server compiles a parameterized query using particular parameter values and reuses the resulting execution plan for subsequent executions. This can become problematic when parameter values have highly different data distributions.

For example, consider an orders table where:

An execution plan optimized for the second customer may perform poorly when reused for the first. In an actual execution plan, inspect the parameter information, including:

A significant difference between these values, combined with skewed data and inconsistent performance, can indicate parameter sensitivity.

An Index Seek is not always better than an Index Scan. SQL Server chooses an access method based on estimated cost, cardinality, available indexes, and the amount of data required. However, certain patterns deserve investigation.

Before creating an index, evaluate existing indexes, write overhead, storage consumption, and whether the proposed index would actually improve the workload.

For example, comparing an integer column with a string parameter can introduce an implicit conversion and prevent an efficient index access path in some circumstances. Similarly, spills to tempdb can indicate that an operator received an insufficient memory grant. These warnings help identify where further investigation is needed.

SQL Server may suggest missing indexes in execution plans. However, these suggestions do not understand the entire indexing strategy of your application.

Before creating a suggested index, consider:

The goal is not to maximize the number of indexes. It is to improve the overall workload.

Once you understand the problem, address the underlying cause. A reasonable troubleshooting order is:

Sometimes the root cause cannot be fixed immediately. For example, a vendor application may generate SQL that cannot be modified without a lengthy release process. SQL Server 2022 introduced Query Store hints, which allow administrators to apply supported query hints without changing application code.

This applies a recompilation hint to the selected Query Store query.

It is important to understand that OPTION (RECOMPILE) is not plan forcing. It instructs SQL Server to compile a new plan for each execution, which can help with parameter-sensitive workloads but also introduces compilation overhead.

Another option is to force a previously successful execution plan.

This tells SQL Server to use the selected historical plan when possible. Plan forcing should be treated as a temporary mitigation rather than a permanent solution. A forced plan may become less efficient as data distributions and workloads change. It may also fail to apply if required database objects or indexes are no longer available.

Since SQL Server 2017, automatic plan correction is also available on supported SQL Server configurations.

Check edition and platform support before enabling automatic tuning.

Even when automatic correction is available, monitor its decisions and validate that the forced plans continue to perform well.

Consider an e-commerce application where the order history endpoint starts responding slowly. Initially, the endpoint responds in approximately 200 milliseconds. After a deployment and a change in workload distribution, response times increase to several seconds. The development team initially suspects application code. However, Query Store reveals something different.

Investigation 1: Identify the expensive query

The query appears near the top of the total-duration report. Its execution count has increased, and its average duration is substantially higher than its historical baseline.

Query Store shows that the query has two historical plans. The newer plan performs significantly more logical reads.

Investigation 3: Inspect the actual execution plan

The team finds that a parameter-sensitive query is using an inefficient plan for customers with large order histories. The actual row counts differ significantly from the estimates.

The team evaluates the available indexes, reviews statistics, and tests a suitable parameter-sensitive query optimization. If an immediate application change is not possible, a Query Store hint or a previously successful plan may provide a temporary mitigation.

The objective is not simply to make one execution faster. It is to restore predictable performance across the workload.

Even with Query Store enabled, several issues can affect the accuracy of your investigation.

1. Query Store stops collecting information

A full Query Store can transition into read-only mode.

Check sys.database_query_store_options regularly, especially actual_state_desc, desired_state_desc, and readonly_reason.

2. Ad hoc workloads inflate storage consumption

Applications that generate many unparameterized queries can create large numbers of distinct query entries. Use an appropriate capture mode and investigate parameterization opportunities.

A reasonable average duration can hide occasional executions that take several seconds. Examine maximum duration, standard deviation, execution counts, and individual runtime intervals before deciding that a plan is healthy.

4. Time zones create misleading correlations

Query Store timestamps are stored in UTC. Convert timestamps appropriately before comparing them with application logs, deployment records, or monitoring dashboards.

5. Historical statistics are not necessarily actual execution plans

Query Store provides valuable plan history and aggregated runtime statistics, but it should not be mistaken for a complete historical record of actual execution plans with actual row counts. Use actual execution plans and appropriate runtime diagnostics when deeper investigation is necessary.

The examples in this article target different SQL Server versions.

Always verify the feature's availability and configuration requirements for your SQL Server edition and deployment environment.

Diagnosing slow SQL queries requires more than identifying expensive operators in an execution plan. The most effective approach combines historical workload information with detailed execution-plan analysis.

The tooling is not the hardest part of SQL Server performance troubleshooting. What separates a ten-minute diagnosis from a three-day investigation is having the historical evidence to understand what changed. Query Store provides that evidence. Execution plans help explain it. Together, they give database engineers a repeatable approach to diagnosing and resolving SQL Server performance problems.

How to Query Data the Professional Way in SQL Server: A Performance-First Guide for Beginners

#9662. The 12 best recipes to bake in October: It’s peak baking season — here’s what to make.

#9657. Ahrefs vs SEMrush: Which SEO Tool Should You Use?

SEMrush and Ahrefs are among the most popular tools in the SEO industry. Both companies have been in business for years and have thousands of customers per month.

If you're a professional SEO or trying to do digital marketing on your own, at some point you'll likely consider using a tool to help with your efforts. Ahrefs and SEMrush are two names that will likely appear on your shortlist.

In this guide, I'm going to help you learn more about these SEO tools and how to choose the one that's best for your purposes.

SEMrush is a popular SEO tool with a wide range of features—it's the leading competitor research service for online marketers. SEMrush's SEO Keyword Magic tool offers over 20 billion Google-approved keywords, which are constantly updated and it's the largest keyword database.

The program was developed in 2007 as SeoQuake is a small Firefox extension

Ahrefs is a leading SEO platform that offers a set of tools to grow your search traffic, research your competitors, and monitor your niche. The company was founded in 2010, and it has become a popular choice among SEO tools. Ahrefs has a keyword index of over 10.3 billion keywords and offers accurate and extensive backlink data updated every 15-30 minutes and it is the world's most extensive backlink index database.

Now that you know a little more about each tool, let's take a look at how they compare. I'll analyze each tool to see how they differ in interfaces, keyword research resources, rank tracking, and competitor analysis.

Ahrefs and SEMrush both offer comprehensive information and quick metrics regarding your website's SEO performance. However, Ahrefs takes a bit more of a hands-on approach to getting your account fully set up, whereas SEMrush's simpler dashboard can give you access to the data you need quickly.

In this section, we provide a brief overview of the elements found on each dashboard and highlight the ease with which you can complete tasks.

The Ahrefs dashboard is less cluttered than that of SEMrush, and its primary menu is at the very top of the page, with a search bar designed only for entering URLs.

Additional features of the Ahrefs platform include:

When you log into the SEMrush Tool, you will find four main modules. These include information about your domains, organic keyword analysis, ad keyword, and site traffic.

Both Ahrefs and SEMrush have user-friendly dashboards, but Ahrefs is less cluttered and easier to navigate. On the other hand, SEMrush offers dozens of extra tools, including access to customer support resources.

When deciding on which dashboard to use, consider what you value in the user interface, and test out both.

If you're looking to track your website's search engine ranking, rank tracking features can help. You can also use them to monitor your competitors.

Let's take a look at Ahrefs vs. SEMrush to see which tool does a better job.

The Ahrefs Rank Tracker is simpler to use. Just type in the domain name and keywords you want to analyze, and it spits out a report showing you the search engine results page (SERP) ranking for each keyword you enter.

Rank Tracker looks at the ranking performance of keywords and compares them with the top rankings for those keywords. Ahrefs also offers:

You'll see metrics that help you understand your visibility, traffic, average position, and keyword difficulty.

It gives you an idea of whether a keyword would be profitable to target or not.

SEMRush offers a tool called Position Tracking. This tool is a project tool—you must set it up as a new project. Below are a few of the most popular features of the SEMrush Position Tracking tool:

The platform provides opportunities to track several SERP features, including Local tracking.

Intuitive reports allow you to track statistics for the pages on your website, as well as the keywords used in those pages.

Identify pages that may be competing with each other using the Cannibalization report.

Ahrefs is a more user-friendly option. It takes seconds to enter a domain name and keywords. From there, you can quickly decide whether to proceed with that keyword or figure out how to rank better for other keywords.

SEMrush allows you to check your mobile rankings and ranking updates daily, which is something Ahrefs does not offer. SEMrush also offers social media rankings, a tool you won't find within the Ahrefs platform. Both are good which one do you like let me know in the comment.

Keyword research is closely related to rank tracking, but it's used for deciding which keywords you plan on using for future content rather than those you use now.

When it comes to SEO, keyword research is the most important thing to consider when comparing the two platforms.

The Ahrefs Keyword Explorer provides you with thousands of keyword ideas and filters search results based on the chosen search engine.

Ahrefs supports several features, including:

SEMrush's Keyword Magic Tool has over 20 billion keywords for Google. You can type in any keyword you want, and a list of suggested keywords will appear.

Both of these tools offer keyword research features and allow users to break down complicated tasks into something that can be understood by beginners and advanced users alike.

If you're interested in keyword suggestions, SEMrush appears to have more keyword suggestions than Ahrefs does. It also continues to add new features, like the Keyword Gap tool and SERP Questions recommendations.

Both platforms offer competitor analysis tools, eliminating the need to come up with keywords off the top of your head. Each tool is useful for finding keywords that will be useful for your competition so you know they will be valuable to you.

Ahrefs' domain comparison tool lets you compare up to five websites (your website and four competitors) side-by-side.it also shows you how your site is ranked against others with metrics such as backlinks, domain ratings, and more.

Use the Competing Domains section to see a list of your most direct competitors, and explore how many keywords matches your competitors have.

To find more information about your competitor, you can look at the Site Explorer and Content Explorer tools and type in their URL instead of yours.

SEMrush provides a variety of insights into your competitors' marketing tactics. The platform enables you to research your competitors effectively. It also offers several resources for competitor analysis including:

Traffic Analytics helps you identify where your audience comes from, how they engage with your site, what devices visitors use to view your site, and how your audiences overlap with other websites.

SEMrush's Organic Research examines your website's major competitors and shows their organic search rankings, keywords they are ranking for, and even if they are ranking for any (SERP) features and more.

The Market Explorer search field allows you to type in a domain and lists websites or articles similar to what you entered. Market Explorer also allows users to perform in-depth data analytics on These companies and markets.

SEMrush wins here because it has more tools dedicated to competitor analysis than Ahrefs. However, Ahrefs offers a lot of functionality in this area, too. It takes a combination of both tools to gain an advantage over your competition.

When it comes to keyword data research, you will become confused about which one to choose.

Both tools are great. Choose the one which meets your requirements and if you have any experience using either Ahrefs or SEMrush let me know in the comment section which works well for you.

Are you searching for an ecomerce platform to help you build an online store and sell products?

In this Sellfy review, we'll talk about how this eCommerce platform can let you sell digital products while keeping full control of your marketing.

And the best part? Starting your business can be done in just five minutes.

Let us then talk about the Sellfy platform and all the benefits it can bring to your business.

Sellfy is an eCommerce solution that allows digital content creators, including writers, illustrators, designers, musicians, and filmmakers, to sell their products online. Sellfy provides a customizable storefront where users can display their digital products and embed "Buy Now" buttons on their website or blog. Sellfy product pages enable users to showcase their products from different angles with multiple images and previews from Soundcloud, Vimeo, and YouTube. Files of up to 2GB can be uploaded to Sellfy, and the company offers unlimited bandwidth and secure file storage. Users can also embed their entire store or individual project widgets in their site, with the ability to preview how widgets will appear before they are displayed.

Sellfy is a powerful e-commerce platform that helps you personalize your online storefront. You can add your logo, change colors, revise navigation, and edit the layout of your store. Sellfy also allows you to create a full shopping cart so customers can purchase multiple items. And Sellfy gives you the ability to set your language or let customers see a translated version of your store based on their location.

Sellfy gives you the option to host your store directly on its platform, add a custom domain to your store, and use it as an embedded storefront on your website. Sellfy also optimizes its store offerings for mobile devices, allowing for a seamless checkout experience.

Sellfy allows creators to host all their products and sell all of their digital products on one platform. Sellfy also does not place storage limits on your store but recommends that files be no larger than 5GB. Creators can sell both standard and subscription-based products in any file format that is supported by the online marketplace. Customers can purchase products instantly after making a purchase – there is no waiting period.

You can organize your store by creating your product categories, sorting by any characteristic you choose. Your title, description, and the image will be included on each product page. In this way, customers can immediately evaluate all of your products. You can offer different pricing options for all of your products, including "pay what you want," in which the price is entirely up to the customer. This option allows you to give customers control over the cost of individual items (without a minimum price) or to set pricing minimums—a good option if you're in a competitive market or when you have higher-end products. You can also offer set prices per product as well as free products to help build your store's popularity.

Sellfy is ideal for selling digital content, such as ebooks. But it does not allow you to copyrighted material (that you don't have rights to distribute).

Sellfy offers several ways to share your store, enabling you to promote your business on different platforms. Sellfy lets you integrate it with your existing website using "buy now" buttons, embed your entire storefront, or embed certain products so you can reach more people. Sellfy also enables you to connect with your Facebook page and YouTube channel, maximizing your visibility.

Sellfy is a simple online platform that allows customers to buy your products directly through your store. Sellfy has two payment processing options: PayPal and Stripe. You will receive instant payments with both of these processors, and your customer data is protected by Sellfy's secure (PCI-compliant) payment security measures. In addition to payment security, Sellfy provides anti-fraud tools to help protect your products including PDF stamping, unique download links, and limited download attempts.

To expand functionality and make your e-commerce store run more efficiently, Sellfy offers several integrations. Google Analytics and Webhooks, as well as integrations with Patreon and Facebook Live Chat, are just a few of the options available. Sellfy allows you to connect to Zapier, which gives you access to hundreds of third-party apps, including tools like Mailchimp, Trello, Salesforce, and more.

Sellfy has its benefits and downsides, but fortunately, the pros outweigh the cons.

In this article, we have taken a look at some of the biggest benefits associated with using sellfy for eCommerce. Once you compare these benefits to what you get with other platforms such as Shopify, you should find that it is worth your time to consider sellfy for your business. #9650. ProWritingAid VS Grammarly: Which Grammar Checker is Better in (2022) ?

Grammarly is a tool that checks for grammatical errors, spelling, and punctuation.it gives you comprehensive feedback on your writing. You can use this tool to proofread and edit articles, blog posts, emails, etc.

Grammarly also detects all types of mistakes, including sentence structure issues and misused words. It also gives you suggestions on style changes, punctuation, spelling, and grammar all are in real-time. The free version covers the basics like identifying grammar and spelling mistakes

whereas the Premium version offers a lot more functionality, it detects plagiarism in your content, suggests word choice, or adds fluency to it.

ProWritingAid is a style and grammar checker for content creators and writers. It helps to optimize word choice, punctuation errors, and common grammar mistakes, providing detailed reports to help you improve your writing.

ProWritingAid can be used as an add-on to WordPress, Gmail, and Google Docs. The software also offers helpful articles, videos, quizzes, and explanations to help improve your writing.

Here are some key features of ProWriting Aid:

Grammarly and ProWritingAid are well-known grammar-checking software. However, if you're like most people who can't decide which to use, here are some different points that may be helpful in your decision.

As both writing assistants are great in their own way, you need to choose the one that suits you best.

Both ProWritingAid and Grammarly are awesome writing tools, without a doubt. but as per my experience, Grammarly is a winner here because Grammarly helps you to review and edit your content. Grammarly highlights all the mistakes in your writing within seconds of copying and pasting the content into Grammarly’s editor or using the software’s native feature in other text editors.

Not only does it identify tiny grammatical and spelling errors, it tells you when you overlook punctuations where they are needed. And, beyond its plagiarism-checking capabilities, Grammarly helps you proofread your content. Even better, the software offers a free plan that gives you access to some of its features.

Sounds like you're biased for Grammarly. Not really that informative if you're already leaning towards one to begin with. Still, it was an interesting read. Tell me, do you use Grammarly with your day-to-day writing/blogging?

I use the paid versions of both Grammarly and Pro Writing Aid. Both of them have issues:- Grammarly IS more focused on nonfiction than fiction. If you're writing fiction, you may find Grammarly's insistence on "Conciseness" annoying. They seem to want to take the soul out of your writing, which is fine for a corporate report or technical manual, but not for your Great American Novel.- Grammarly pushes features on users that are not ready for prime time. It doesn't matter that you never agreed to be a beta tester for them; you get to do it anyway.- Pro Writing Aid actually counts the occurrences of words in your document and tells you when a word has been overused compared to published literature. Grammarly, on the other hand, seems hell-bent to remove certain words that it has deemed overused from the language, whether or not they're actually overused in your document.- Grammarly's Clarity function is simply horrible. It mangles sentences and changes their meaning. Sometimes the result of its suggestion is unintelligible garbage.- Grammarly allows you to turn off some checks, but not all of them. Unfortunately, the ones you cannot turn off are some of the most irritating (such as that horrible "Clarity"). On the other hand, Pro Writing Aid lets you choose which checks you use.- Pro Writing Aid has a mediocre command of American English (it's a British product). The app insists on rules of grammar and spelling that are outright wrong, per Merriam-Webster, the Chicago Manual of Style, and modern usage as shown by Google Books Ngram. At one point, Pro Writing Aid insisted that American English did not include the words "holiday" and "autumn," that "vacation" and "fall" must be used instead.- Pro Writing Aid's rules for commas are 100 percent consistent with the way I learned them in high school--50 years ago! They do not reflect modern usage. Grammarly is much better at this.- Pro Writing Aid seems to waste their limited resources on tweaking their UI. Their UI most definitely could use improvement, but these changes are not great improvements; they only serve to confuse users. Their resources would be better spent fixing the many functional problems in their app.- Some of Pro Writing Aid's checks are completely useless, as they do not take context into consideration. For example, an ordinary word would not be capitalized as part of a narrative, but would be as part of a title (for example, "professor." But if you capitalize correctly for context, Pro Writing Aid dings you for "Inconsistent capitalization." Similar issues exist with hyphenation consistency check.Each of these applications has its strengths as well as considerable weaknesses. I will say that both of them are light-years better than the execrable grammar checker in Microsoft Word, but that's damning with faint praise.

#9645. What is Blockchain: Everything You Need to Know (2022)

Imagine a world in which you can do transactions and many other things without having to give your personal information. A world in which you don’t need to rely on banks or governments anymore. Sounds amazing, right? That’s exactly what blockchain technology allows us to do.

It’s like your computer’s hard drive. blockchain is a technology that lets you store data in digital blocks, which are connected together like links in a chain.

Blockchain technology was originally invented in 1991 by two mathematicians, Stuart Haber and W. Scot Stornetta. They first proposed the system to ensure that timestamps could not be tampered with.

A few years later, in 1998, software developer Nick Szabo proposed using a similar kind of technology to secure a digital payments system he called “Bit Gold.” However, this innovation was not adopted until Satoshi Nakamoto claimed to have invented the first Blockchain and Bitcoin.

A blockchain is a distributed database shared between the nodes of a computer network. It saves information in digital format. Many people first heard of blockchain technology when they started to look up information about bitcoin.

Blockchain is used in cryptocurrency systems to ensure secure, decentralized records of transactions.

Blockchain allowed people to guarantee the fidelity and security of a record of data without the need for a third party to ensure accuracy.

To understand how a blockchain works, Consider these basic steps:

Let’s get to know more about the blockchain.

Blockchain records digital information and distributes it across the network without changing it. The information is distributed among many users and stored in an immutable, permanent ledger that can't be changed or destroyed. That's why blockchain is also called "Distributed Ledger Technology" or DLT.

And that’s the beauty of it! The process may seem complicated, but it’s done in minutes with modern technology. And because technology is advancing rapidly, I expect things to move even more quickly than ever.

Even though blockchain is integral to cryptocurrency, it has other applications. For example, blockchain can be used for storing reliable data about transactions. Many people confuse blockchain with cryptocurrencies like bitcoin and ethereum.

Blockchain already being adopted by some big-name companies, such as Walmart, AIG, Siemens, Pfizer, and Unilever. For example, IBM's Food Trust uses blockchain to track food's journey before reaching its final destination.

Although some of you may consider this practice excessive, food suppliers and manufacturers adhere to the policy of tracing their products because bacteria such as E. coli and Salmonella have been found in packaged foods. In addition, there have been isolated cases where dangerous allergens such as peanuts have accidentally been introduced into certain products.

Tracing and identifying the sources of an outbreak is a challenging task that can take months or years. Thanks to the Blockchain, however, companies now know exactly where their food has been—so they can trace its location and prevent future outbreaks.

Blockchain technology allows systems to react much faster in the event of a hazard. It also has many other uses in the modern world.

Blockchain technology is safe, even if it’s public. People can access the technology using an internet connection.

Have you ever been in a situation where you had all your data stored at one place and that one secure place got compromised? Wouldn't it be great if there was a way to prevent your data from leaking out even when the security of your storage systems is compromised?

Blockchain technology provides a way of avoiding this situation by using multiple computers at different locations to store information about transactions. If one computer experiences problems with a transaction, it will not affect the other nodes.

Instead, other nodes will use the correct information to cross-reference your incorrect node. This is called “Decentralization,” meaning all the information is stored in multiple places.

Blockchain guarantees your data's authenticity—not just its accuracy, but also its irreversibility. It can also be used to store data that are difficult to register, like legal contracts, state identifications, or a company's product inventory.

Blockchain has many advantages and disadvantages.

I’ll answer the most frequently asked questions about blockchain in this section.

Blockchain is not a cryptocurrency but a technology that makes cryptocurrencies possible. It's a digital ledger that records every transaction seamlessly.

Yes, blockchain can be theoretically hacked, but it is a complicated task to be achieved. A network of users constantly reviews it, which makes hacking the blockchain difficult.

Coinbase Global is currently the biggest blockchain company in the world. The company runs a commendable infrastructure, services, and technology for the digital currency economy.

Blockchain is a decentralized technology. It’s a chain of distributed ledgers connected with nodes. Each node can be any electronic device. Thus, one owns blockhain.

Bitcoin is a cryptocurrency, which is powered by Blockchain technology while Blockchain is a distributed ledger of cryptocurrency

Generally a database is a collection of data which can be stored and organized using a database management system. The people who have access to the database can view or edit the information stored there. The client-server network architecture is used to implement databases. whereas a blockchain is a growing list of records, called blocks, stored in a distributed system. Each block contains a cryptographic hash of the previous block, timestamp and transaction information. Modification of data is not allowed due to the design of the blockchain. The technology allows decentralized control and eliminates risks of data modification by other parties.

Blockchain has a wide spectrum of applications and, over the next 5-10 years, we will likely see it being integrated into all sorts of industries. From finance to healthcare, blockchain could revolutionize the way we store and share data. Although there is some hesitation to adopt blockchain systems right now, that won't be the case in 2022-2023 (and even less so in 2026). Once people become more comfortable with the technology and understand how it can work for them, owners, CEOs and entrepreneurs alike will be quick to leverage blockchain technology for their own gain.
